probe.format_note: 9:16 (720x1278, non-square SAR close to 1), 962 frames, H.264; stereo HE-AACv2 44.1 kHz music bed (not analysed for tempo). The frame is a 'making-of' presentation: three rounded cards stacked vertically on a light blue-grey background with bubbles and large tilted translucent blue rectangles. Top card (about y 150-455 px) = the editor viewport of the same animation with selection boxes, anchor points and motion paths; middle card (about y 455-815 px, the widest, with a soft drop shadow) = the finished render; bottom dark card (about y 815-1110 px) = a keyframe timeline whose playhead advances. The outer frame and the three cards never move; all motion is inside the cards. The reading table below describes the finished render in the middle card; the outer frame is read separately as 'frame_device'.

mode.alt_film_mode: UI when the package launches an app, a tool or a workflow (the reference is an app promo: problem in words, then product, then logo)
mode.why: third-party film of unknown origin: borrow the motion language and look only (word-by-word soft type on an off-white card, blur-in/blur-out phrase changes, a glossy 3D icon popping between words, 3D device and ribbon shots, glass card stacks, push-in into type, letter-by-letter logo build), never its shots one by one, its brands, products, people, copy or figures (owner note); a voiceover package defaults to REEL, and the reference is a short problem → solution → logo voice-style reel

ignored.why: all third-party brands and marks: the 'phia' wordmark and tagline 'Your personal fashion headquarters', amazon, Nike swoosh, Louis Vuitton, Coach bag names, App Store and Chrome Web Store badges; never reused

all English copy ('Ever bought something', 'then found it', '$500 cheaper a week later?', 'we've all been there.', 'Prices change.', 'Discounts come and go.', 'Thousands of stores.', 'One frustrated shopper.', 'Automatically scans deals across', '10,000+ sites', 'No more switching tabs.', 'No more guessing games.', 'Just smart shopping - made simple.') and its figures ($500, 10,000+); never reused as text, our words and numbers come only from the approved package
product photos (handbags) and photos of a real model inside the phone screens and the full-frame product grid; never reused; the screen slots may hold only owner assets or code-drawn UI

the top editor-viewport card (selection handles, motion paths) and the bottom timeline card are screen captures of third-party animation software; their contents are never reused, only the stacked-floating-card frame as a look (see frame_device)

method: ffprobe; ffmpeg contact sheets fps=2 of the full frame at 240 px, tile 6x2 (6 sheets, all viewed; frame time = (sheet-1)*6 + index*0.5 s); scene detect gt(scene,0.3) on the full frame found no cuts (the outer frame is static), so scene detect gt(scene,0.12) on a crop of the middle render card (crop=640:340:40:465) found the only hard changes at 12.23, 14.9, 16.73 and 20.8 s; dense sheets fps=10 of the middle card at 0-2, 6.4-9.4, 14.5-17.5, 19.8-22.8 and 25.8-28.8 s (5 sheets, all viewed). Spans between those cuts come from the 0.5 s and 0.1 s sheets, accurate to about ±0.1-0.25 s. Colours read by eye, not sampled. Music not analysed.

frame_device.what: Three rounded cards stacked vertically and overlapping slightly (top card partly behind the middle one, bottom card behind the middle one), all static, on a light background. The middle card is the widest and brightest (off-white), with a large soft drop shadow; the top card is a slightly greyer, narrower card; the bottom card is near-black.
frame_device.background: light blue-grey to white vertical gradient with soft blue glows at the corners, small outlined blue bubbles of varied size, and big tilted translucent blue rounded rectangles (glass slabs) at the edges, slightly blurred
frame_device.reusable: yes, as a look: content shown inside a floating off-white card with a soft shadow, over a calm light-blue bubble-and-glass background; the card stack suggests 'layers' or 'behind the scenes'. Never reuse the editor viewport or timeline contents; if a stack is used, the other cards hold our own content (a preview, a caption, a progress strip).

visual_language: A calm, soft, mostly typographic app promo presented as a making-of: the finished film sits in a floating off-white card above an editor viewport and below-it timeline, on a light blue bubble-and-glass background. Medium: kinetic type in code for more than half of the running time, broken by a few dimensional beats (a glossy 3D icon between words, a tunnel of phones, a 3D phone wrapped in glossy ribbons, a dark glowing stack of glass cards, a conveyor of glossy tiles, a field of frosted windows). Typography: one clean neutral sans, small (about 3% of card height) for most lines, medium weight, near-black with one or two words in blue; the answer lines are fully blue (sometimes a blue gradient); one bold large headline and one bold white number; the end wordmark is a serif italic. Rhythm: about 17 beats in 32 s (average about 1.9 s), almost no hard cuts (four in the whole film); phrase changes are soft blur-outs and blur-ins on the voice, words land about every 0.2-0.25 s; type beats alternate with 3D or UI beats roughly every 2-3 lines. Palette: off-white, near-black, one blue family (royal, sky, pale), one dark navy contrast scene with cyan glow. Signature moments: the 3D icon popping between two words, the phone tunnel around a tiny line, the ribbons wrapping the phone, the glass card stack rising on navy, the push through a big number, the promise line pushed in until it is cropped, the letter-by-letter wordmark.
look: Mixed: flat clean type on a flat off-white card for the type beats (no texture, no shadow on text); real 3D for the dimensional beats — glossy blue plastic icon with highlights and a soft glow, phones with real perspective, glossy royal-blue and matte white ribbons under soft studio light with soft shadows and depth blur, frosted glass cards with backdrop blur and rim light on a deep navy glowing ground, glossy rounded tiles with soft drop shadows, frosted pale-blue windows with parallax. Motion blur on fast moves (phone slide-in, whip push, flying dot) and gaussian blur as the standard phrase transition. Outer frame: floating rounded cards with large soft shadows over a light blue-grey gradient with outlined bubbles and tilted translucent blue glass slabs.
code_translation: Code-native with real 3D. Type beats: DOM text in the brand font, words split into spans; each word animates scale 0.7 → 1, translateY +6 px → 0, filter blur(6px) → 0, colour blue → final, about 0.25 s ease-out, staggered on the voice word timings; phrase exit = blur(0 → 10px) + opacity 1 → 0 in about 0.2 s; whole-phrase blur-in for answer lines. 3D beats are built as real 3D in three.js (never flattened into 2D shapes): the glossy icon (MeshPhysicalMaterial, clearcoat, environment light, soft glow), the phone tunnel (rounded device planes on a cylinder, camera dolly with roll), the phone with ribbons (ribbon as an extruded curve or tube with a sliding texture or vertex offset, two materials, soft shadows, depth of field as blur), the glass card stack (transmission or backdrop-blur planes with rim light, additive cyan sparkle sprites). 2.5D beats (window field, tile conveyor) in CSS 3D with soft shadows and parallax. Motion blur by frame blending or directional blur on fast moves. Push-in into type by scaling the type layer with ease-in-out and a short blur. Logo build: letters as spans scaling in one by one (our own logo and outro rules apply). The outer card stack: three rounded divs with large soft shadows over a CSS gradient with SVG bubbles and blurred translucent rounded rectangles. Screen contents of devices: owner assets or code-drawn UI.
code_buildable_note: 32.13 s total; only r1-s9 (0.6 s full-card product-photo grid) is photo-dependent; 3D renders count as buildable (D55); photos inside phone screens elsewhere are image slots filled with owner assets or code-drawn UI.
continuity: One stage for the whole film: everything happens inside the same floating off-white card, so even the 3D and dark scenes read as one continuous piece.
Soft blur-out / blur-in instead of cuts between phrases: the previous line dissolves in place and the next one materialises at the same centre, so the eye never has to move.
Word-by-word build synced to the voice, with the newest word still tinted in the accent colour while it settles — the colour marks 'now'.
A line splits apart to make room for an object that pops in between its words, then the whole group leaves together (text and object as one unit).
Push or rise exits: a group drifts up and out of the stage while the next object slides in from the bottom with motion blur, so one scene pushes the other out.
Breath beat: one faint word on an empty stage, then the next big scene builds around it instead of cutting to it.
Camera through an object: a cut into a screen close-up followed by a fast pull-back reveals the object in its world; a push into a fold of the hero object blurs into haze, which opens the next scene.
Push through a big figure: the number grows until it overflows the frame and the zoom carries the camera into the next scene's haze.
Light wash-out: a dark contrast scene brightens and desaturates to the white stage, so the return to type is soft.
Repetition shown as many identical objects (a ring of devices, a conveyor of tiles, a field of windows) around or behind one small line of text.
The final promise line is built small, then pushed in until cropped; the logo then writes itself letter by letter on the same empty stage.
risks: Third-party film of unknown origin: ADAPT only. Never copy its brand, wordmark, product names, third-party logos (amazon, Nike, Louis Vuitton, Coach, store badges), product or model photos, copy, figures or the shot order one by one.

The making-of frame (editor viewport card and timeline card around the render) is not the film itself: a film using it fills the extra cards with our own content or drops them; never show third-party software screens.

Text is very small in the reference (about 3% of card height inside a card that is about half the frame): readability ranks above the reference; Persian lines must meet the minimum sizes and safe zones in safe-zones.md, so type is set larger, or the card is enlarged, for 9:16.

Word-by-word reveals and the blur-in per word must keep Persian words whole and correctly joined: animate whole words (never letters) for Persian, and keep the right-to-left build order (rtl-grammar.md). The letter-by-letter logo build applies only to a Latin wordmark or as a whole-logo reveal; the brand logo outro rules win.
Leftward drifts, the tile conveyor moving left and the push-in crop to the left read left → right: for Persian the directions follow references/rtl-grammar.md.

Real 3D beats (ribbons, phone tunnel, glossy icon, glass stack) are costlier to build and render than type; motion-build must use three.js with lights, soft shadows and depth blur rather than flat 2D stand-ins (D55).

Reference colours (off-white, near-black, blue family, navy with cyan glow, pale-blue background) map onto brand colour roles (light background, text, primary/accent, dark background); never used as literal hex values. Colours were read by eye, not sampled.
The reference has its own music bed; our cuts and reveals follow the voiceover first, and L6 sets sound. Tempo was not analysed.
Any figure shown big (as in r1-s13) must be a sourced value from the package and must end exactly on it (data-viz.md), in Persian digits.
